diagnostic.q: f(x) = 2x + 1, g(x) = x^2. Find f(g(3)) and g(f(3)).
sin 30 deg + cos 60 deg + tan 45 deg = ?
sin t = 3/5 with t in quadrant I. Find cos 2t.
int from 0 to pi/2 of sin^2 x dx = ?
1% have a disease. Test: 99% sensitive, 5% false positives. P(disease | positive)?
X uniform on [0, 2]. E[X] and Var(X)?
One Newton-Raphson step for x^2 - 2 = 0 from x0 = 1.
Simpson 1/3 rule with 2 strips for int 0..2 x^2 dx: result?
X(t) = A cos(wt), A zero-mean with variance s^2. Mean and R(t1,t2)? Is it WSS?
diagnostic.a: Mean 0, R = s^2 cos(w t1) cos(w t2); not WSS

diagnostic.q: Is the function f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 5 convex, and where is its minimum?

nodes.name: Arithmetic and mental maths
outcomes: Squares 1-25 and tables to 20 recalled instantly
Two-digit products by splitting and difference of squares
Fractions, percentages and decimals converted in the head
Estimate any answer to 1 significant figure before computing
Powers of 2/10 and decibels without a calculator

contracts.title: Squares 11-25 from memory
contracts.context: Fast number facts free working memory for the real problem (algebra, integrals). Squares come up in every exam.
steps: Write 11 to 25 in a column.
Say each square aloud and write it, timer running, no checking.
Check against the key, star every miss.
Re-test only the starred ones after 10 minutes.
contracts.hint: For numbers ending in 5: n5 squared = n(n+1) followed by 25, so 35^2 = 3x4 = 12 -> 1225. Otherwise use (a+b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2: 17^2 = 289.

contracts.title: Two-digit products in your head
contracts.context: Splitting and difference of squares turn hard products into easy ones.
steps: Compute without paper: 47x23, 38x42, 64x15, 99x37, 56x54.
Say the method you used for each (split, round-and-adjust, or difference of squares).
Check, then redo misses with a different method.

contracts.title: Percent, fraction, decimal flips
contracts.context: Probability and circuit questions are full of these conversions.
steps: 3/8 as a decimal
contracts.hint: 10% then halve for 5%. 12.5% = 1/8. Common denominator 12 for the last one.

contracts.title: Estimate first, then compute
contracts.context: Estimation catches the silly errors that cost exam marks.
steps: Estimate to 1 significant figure, then compute: sqrt(50), e^3, 2^10, ln 2, pi^2, 3.9x5.1.
Write estimate and exact side by side.
contracts.hint: sqrt(50) is a bit above 7 (7^2=49). e^3 = e x e x e ~ 2.72 x 7.39.
contracts.success_check: Exact within 2%: 7.07, 20.1, 1024, 0.693, 9.87, 19.89; every estimate within 20% of exact.

contracts.title: Powers of 2 and decibels (ECE)
contracts.context: dB, bits and memory sizes appear in every ECE paper and in VLSI work.
steps: How many dB is doubling an amplitude? Doubling a power?
contracts.hint: Power uses 10log10, amplitude uses 20log10. log10(2) ~ 0.301.
contracts.success_check: 1024, 65536, ~3 dB, 20 dB, 30 dB; amplitude x2 = ~6.02 dB, power x2 = ~3.01 dB.

contracts.title: Sign and order-of-operations traps
contracts.context: Most of his lost marks are sign slips, not concept gaps.
steps: For each wrong one, write the rule you broke in the error log.
contracts.hint: Exponent binds before the minus sign: -3^2 = -(3^2). Division and multiplication go left to right.

contracts.title: Daily 5-minute mixed sprint
contracts.context: The warm-up of every maths session. Mixed and timed, so it is retrieval practice, not rereading.
steps: Generate 20 mixed items (2-digit x 2-digit, fraction add, % of, square, power of 2) or let JARVIS give them.
5 minutes, no calculator.
Log score and time.
contracts.hint: Skip and come back; do not stall on one item.

nodes.name: Algebra
outcomes: Solve linear, quadratic and simultaneous equations without sign errors
Factorise quadratics, cubics and differences of squares/cubes
Use exponent and log laws fluently
Split rational functions into partial fractions (needed for integrals and Laplace)
Solve inequalities and modulus equations

contracts.title: Linear equations clean-up
contracts.context: Class 9 algebra, the floor under everything else.
steps: Solve 3(x-2) = 2x+5.
Substitute each answer back to check.
contracts.hint: Clear fractions by multiplying both sides by the LCM (6) first. Expand brackets before moving terms.
contracts.success_check: x = 11, x = 1, x = -1, each verified by substitution.

contracts.title: Factorise like a machine
contracts.context: Factorising is the step that unlocks limits, partial fractions and roots.
contracts.hint: For ax^2+bx+c find two numbers with product ac and sum b (for 6x^2+x-2: 4 and -3). a^3-b^3 = (a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2).

contracts.title: Quadratic formula and discriminant
contracts.context: Second-order ODEs and circuit damping all reduce to a quadratic.
steps: Solve x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0.
Solve 2x^2 + 3x + 5 = 0 (say what kind of roots).
Find k so that x^2 + kx + 9 = 0 has equal roots.
contracts.hint: Discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac: D>0 two real, D=0 equal, D<0 complex pair.

contracts.title: Exponents and logarithms
contracts.context: Logs are how dB, entropy and exponential decay are handled.
steps: Simplify (x^3 . x^-5)/x^-4.
Evaluate log2 32 + log10 0.01.
Solve log3 x + log3 (x-8) = 2.
contracts.hint: log a + log b = log ab. Always check the domain: log needs a positive argument.
contracts.success_check: x^2; x = 4; 3; x = 9 (x = -1 rejected because log of a negative number is undefined).

contracts.title: Simultaneous equations, 2 and 3 unknowns
contracts.context: This is Gaussian elimination by hand; Unit IV (LU, Gauss-Seidel) builds on it.
steps: Solve 2x + 3y = 12, x - y = 1.
Solve x+y+z=6, x-y+z=2, 2x+y-z=1.
Check by substitution.
contracts.hint: Subtract the first two 3-variable equations to kill x and z at once.

contracts.title: Partial fractions
contracts.context: Needed for integration (Unit I-type problems) and inverse Laplace/Z transforms.
steps: Worked-example fading: copy the cover-up method for the first, do the second alone.
contracts.hint: Cover-up: A = value of the rest at x = 1, so A = 1/(1+2). Repeated factor needs A/(x+1) + B/(x+1)^2.

contracts.title: Inequalities and modulus
contracts.context: Regions of convergence and stability conditions are inequalities.
steps: Solve |2x - 3| < 5.
Solve x^2 - 5x + 6 > 0.
Draw both on a number line.
contracts.hint: |u| < 5 means -5 < u < 5. For the quadratic, factor and test a point in each interval.

contracts.title: Productive struggle: JEE-style algebra
contracts.context: Hard problems first, help second. Attempt 15 minutes before opening the hint.
steps: If a+b = 5 and ab = 3, find a^2+b^2 and a^3+b^3.
If a, b are roots of x^2 - 3x + 1 = 0, find a^2+b^2 and 1/a + 1/b.
Then try two algebra questions from a JEE Advanced paper (math.r.jee_adv_archive).
contracts.hint: Substitute u = x^2. Use (a+b)^2 = a^2+2ab+b^2 and (a+b)^3 = a^3+b^3+3ab(a+b). For roots, sum = 3 and product = 1.
contracts.success_check: x = +/-1, +/-2; 19 and 80; 7 and 3. Written attempt of at least 15 minutes on the JEE questions before reading any solution.

nodes.name: Functions and graphs
outcomes: Compose and invert functions, state domains
Sketch the 8 parent graphs and their shifts/stretches from memory
Classify even/odd/periodic functions
Read exponential decay (RC, tau) and unit-step signals

contracts.title: Composition, inverse, domain
contracts.context: Function language is how signals and systems are written.
steps: f(x) = 2x+1, g(x) = x^2: find f(g(3)) and g(f(3)).
Find the inverse of f(x) = (x-1)/3.
Domain of sqrt(x-2)/(x-5).
contracts.hint: Inside out for composition. For an inverse swap x and y, then solve for y.

contracts.title: Parent graphs from memory
contracts.context: Seeing the shape before calculating prevents nonsense answers.
steps: Sketch y = x^2, x^3, 1/x, sqrt x, |x|, e^x, ln x, sin x on one sheet without looking.
Mark intercepts and asymptotes.
Compare with OpenStax Precalculus chapter 1/6 figures.
contracts.hint: e^x passes (0,1) with asymptote y=0; ln x passes (1,0) with asymptote x=0; 1/x has both axes as asymptotes.
contracts.success_check: All 8 shapes correct with intercepts and asymptotes marked.

contracts.title: Transformations
contracts.context: Time shift and scaling of signals are graph transformations.
steps: Write the vertex/corner and direction for each.
contracts.hint: f(x-3) moves right by 3; a minus outside flips vertically; f(-x) flips horizontally.
contracts.success_check: Vertex (3,1) opening up and narrower; corner at (-2,0) opening down; decaying exponential through (0,1).

contracts.title: Even, odd, periodic
contracts.context: Fourier series shortcuts depend on symmetry.
steps: Classify x^3, cos x, x^2 + x, |sin x| (give period).
Split e^x into even and odd parts.
contracts.hint: Even part = (f(x)+f(-x))/2, odd part = (f(x)-f(-x))/2.
contracts.success_check: odd, even, neither, even with period pi; even part cosh x, odd part sinh x.

contracts.title: Exponential decay in an RC circuit
contracts.context: The single most used function in ECE.
steps: v(t) = 5 e^(-t/tau), R = 1 kOhm, C = 1 uF. Find tau.
Find v at t = tau.
Find the time to fall to half.
contracts.hint: tau = RC. e^-1 ~ 0.368. Half-life = tau ln 2.

contracts.title: Unit step, ramp, rectangle
contracts.context: Signals papers build everything from u(t).
steps: Sketch u(t), r(t) = t u(t), u(t) - u(t-1).
Sketch x(t) = u(t) - 2u(t-1) + u(t-2).
contracts.hint: Each u(t-a) switches on at t = a; add the pieces interval by interval.

contracts.title: Productive struggle: count solutions with graphs
contracts.context: Hard-problem habit: draw before you solve.
steps: How many real solutions does e^x = x + 2 have?
contracts.hint: Study g(x) = e^x - x - 2: where is its minimum and is it negative there? For the modulus, think distance on the number line.
contracts.success_check: Two solutions (g has a minimum -1 at x = 0 and goes to +infinity both sides); every x in [1,3].

nodes.name: Trigonometry
outcomes: Exact values and radian conversion
Pythagorean, double- and compound-angle identities
Product-to-sum (modulation sidebands)
Solve trig equations on an interval
Write a sin t + b cos t as R sin(t + phi)

contracts.title: Exact-value table
contracts.context: Every calculus and phasor question uses these values.
steps: Fill sin, cos, tan for 0, 30, 45, 60, 90 degrees from memory.
Convert each to radians.
Compute sin 30 + cos 60 + tan 45.
contracts.hint: sin goes sqrt(0)/2, sqrt(1)/2, sqrt(2)/2, sqrt(3)/2, sqrt(4)/2; cos is the reverse.
contracts.success_check: Table fully correct; pi/6, pi/4, pi/3, pi/2; sum = 2.

contracts.title: Pythagorean and double angle
contracts.context: Integrals of sin^2 and cos^2 need these.
steps: sin t = 3/5, t in quadrant I: find cos t, cos 2t, sin 2t.
Write cos 2t three ways.
contracts.hint: cos 2t = 1 - 2 sin^2 t = 2 cos^2 t - 1 = cos^2 t - sin^2 t.

contracts.title: Compound angles
contracts.context: Phase shifts are compound angles.
steps: sin 75, cos 15, tan 15 exactly.

contracts.title: Product-to-sum = AM sidebands
contracts.context: Mixers and AM modulation (Digital Communication this semester) are product-to-sum.
steps: Derive sin A cos B = (1/2)[sin(A+B) + sin(A-B)].
Expand cos(1000t) cos(100t) and list the output frequencies.
contracts.hint: Add the expansions of cos(A+B) and cos(A-B).

contracts.title: Solve trig equations on [0, 2pi)
contracts.context: Typical exam item; tests factorising and the unit circle together.
steps: Solve 2 sin^2 x - sin x - 1 = 0 for x in [0, 2pi).
contracts.hint: Let s = sin x and factorise: (2s + 1)(s - 1) = 0.

contracts.title: Amplitude-phase form
contracts.context: Two phasors adding is exactly this.
steps: Write 3 sin t + 4 cos t as R sin(t + phi).
State the max and min of 3 sin t - 4 cos t.
contracts.hint: R cos phi = 3, R sin phi = 4, so R = 5.

contracts.title: Productive struggle: find sin 18 deg exactly
contracts.context: A JEE classic: no formula sheet has it, you build it.
steps: Let t = 18 deg so 5t = 90. Work 15 minutes before the hint.
Then do two trig questions from a JEE Advanced paper.
contracts.hint: 2t = 90 - 3t, so sin 2t = cos 3t. Expand, divide by cos t, get a quadratic in sin t.

nodes.name: Complex numbers and phasors
outcomes: Add, multiply, divide and take modulus/argument
Move between Cartesian, polar and e^(j theta)
Use De Moivre for powers and roots
Do AC circuit phasor and impedance arithmetic

contracts.title: Complex arithmetic
contracts.context: Every AC circuit, filter and Fourier result is complex arithmetic.
steps: |3+4i| and its conjugate.
contracts.hint: Divide by multiplying top and bottom by the conjugate of the bottom.

contracts.title: Polar and Euler form
contracts.context: e^(j theta) is the language of signals.
steps: Write 1+i, -1, sqrt3 + i in polar form.
Convert 2 e^(i pi/3) to Cartesian.
contracts.hint: r = sqrt(a^2+b^2), theta = atan2(b, a). Check the quadrant.
contracts.success_check: sqrt2 e^(i pi/4), e^(i pi), 2 e^(i pi/6); 1 + i sqrt3.

contracts.title: De Moivre: powers and roots
contracts.context: Roots of unity are the DFT twiddle factors.
steps: The three cube roots of 1.
contracts.hint: Raise r to the power and multiply the angle. Roots: angles 2 pi k / 3.

contracts.title: Phasor addition
contracts.context: Adding sinusoids of the same frequency is adding complex numbers.
steps: v1 = 10 cos(wt), v2 = 10 cos(wt - 90 deg). Find v1 + v2.
contracts.hint: Phasors 10 and -10j.

contracts.title: Impedance
contracts.context: Network analysis and filters.
steps: R = 3 Ohm in series with X_L = 4 Ohm at 10 V: find Z, |Z|, current and its phase.
contracts.hint: Z = R + jX. Current lags in an inductive circuit.
contracts.success_check: Z = 3 + 4j, |Z| = 5 Ohm, I = 2 A lagging by 53.13 deg.

contracts.title: Complex roots of a quadratic
contracts.context: Underdamped circuits have complex poles.
steps: Solve z^2 + 2z + 5 = 0 and plot the roots.
Check sum and product of roots.
contracts.hint: Sum of roots = -b/a, product = c/a.

contracts.title: Productive struggle: sum of cosines
contracts.context: This is the DFT/Dirichlet-kernel computation in disguise.
steps: Find cos t + cos 2t + ... + cos nt in closed form.
Check your formula with n = 1 and n = 2.
contracts.hint: It is the real part of the geometric series e^(it) + ... + e^(int). Factor e^(i(n+1)t/2) out of the result.
contracts.success_check: sin(nt/2) cos((n+1)t/2) / sin(t/2), verified for n = 1 (gives cos t).

nodes.name: Calculus: limits and differentiation
outcomes: Evaluate standard limits incl. L'Hopital
Differentiate with product, quotient and chain rules
Find tangents, rates, maxima and minima
Write Taylor series of e^x, sin, cos, ln(1+x)
Take partial derivatives

contracts.title: Standard limits
contracts.context: Limits decide continuity, derivatives and convergence.
steps: lim x->0 sin(3x)/x
lim n->inf (1 + 1/n)^n
contracts.hint: sin u / u -> 1; factor and cancel; divide top and bottom by the highest power.

contracts.title: Derivative rules drill
contracts.context: Fluency here is half of every engineering maths paper.
steps: d/dx x^2 e^(3x)
d/dx ln(sin x)
d/dx sin(x^2)
contracts.hint: Product: u'v + uv'. Quotient: (u'v - uv')/v^2. Chain: outer' x inner'.

contracts.title: First principles
contracts.context: Knowing where the rules come from (3Blue1Brown ch. 2-3).
steps: Use lim h->0 (f(x+h) - f(x))/h for f = x^2 and f = 1/x.
contracts.hint: Expand (x+h)^2; for 1/x put over a common denominator.

contracts.title: Tangents and rates
contracts.context: Current is the rate of change of charge.
steps: Tangent to y = x^3 - 3x at x = 2.
q(t) = CV(1 - e^(-t/RC)): find i = dq/dt.
contracts.hint: Slope = y'(2). Point-slope form.

contracts.title: Maxima and minima
contracts.context: Optimisation for ML starts here.
steps: Find max and min of f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1.
Squares of side x cut from a 12 cm square sheet to make an open box: maximise volume.
contracts.hint: Set f' = 0, use f'' for the type. V = x(12 - 2x)^2.
contracts.success_check: Max 5 at x = 1, min 1 at x = 3; x = 2 cm gives 128 cm^3.

contracts.title: L'Hopital and Taylor series
contracts.context: Taylor series are how calculators, small-signal models and linearisation work.
steps: lim x->0 (1 - cos x)/x^2
Write e^x, sin x, cos x, ln(1+x) up to x^3.
Approximate sin(0.1).
contracts.hint: Apply L'Hopital twice, or use cos x ~ 1 - x^2/2.

contracts.title: Partial derivatives
contracts.context: The bridge to gradients (Unit II) and to ML.
steps: f(x,y) = x^2 y + sin(xy): find f_x and f_y.
contracts.hint: Treat the other variable as a constant.
contracts.success_check: f_x = 2xy + y cos(xy); f_y = x^2 + x cos(xy).

contracts.title: Productive struggle: JEE limits and derivatives
contracts.context: 15 minutes of real struggle before any hint.
steps: lim x->0 (e^x - 1 - x)/x^2
d/dx x^x
Slope of x^2 + y^2 = 25 at (3,4)
Why is |x| not differentiable at 0?
Then two calculus questions from JEE Advanced (math.r.jee_adv_archive).
contracts.hint: Taylor-expand e^x. Take logs for x^x. Differentiate implicitly. Compare left and right slopes.
contracts.success_check: 1/2; x^x (1 + ln x); -3/4; left slope -1 != right slope +1.

nodes.name: Integration (incl. Beta and Gamma)
outcomes: Recall the standard integrals table
Integrate by substitution, parts and partial fractions
Use definite-integral properties (odd/even, King's rule)
Compute area, energy and RMS
Evaluate Beta and Gamma integrals (JAS 401 Unit I)

contracts.title: Standard integrals from memory
contracts.context: Retrieval, not rereading: write the table blank, then check.
steps: Write integrals of x^n, 1/x, e^(ax), sin, cos, sec^2, 1/(1+x^2), 1/sqrt(1-x^2).
Differentiate each answer to check it.
contracts.hint: Every integral can be checked by differentiating.
contracts.success_check: All 8 correct incl. ln|x|, tan x, arctan x, arcsin x.

contracts.title: Substitution
contracts.context: The most used technique.
steps: int 2x cos(x^2) dx
int e^(3x+1) dx
int x/(x^2+1) dx
int tan x dx
contracts.hint: Pick u as the inside function whose derivative is also present.

contracts.title: Integration by parts (worked-example fading)
contracts.context: Fading: first problem fully worked in MIT 18.01SC, then you fill the last step, then you do it alone.
steps: int x e^x dx
int ln x dx
int x sin x dx
int e^x sin x dx
contracts.hint: LIATE picks u. For e^x sin x apply parts twice and solve for the integral.
contracts.success_check: (x-1)e^x; x ln x - x; -x cos x + sin x; e^x (sin x - cos x)/2.

contracts.title: Partial-fraction integrals
contracts.context: Reuses math.algebra.c06.

contracts.title: Definite-integral properties
contracts.context: Properties turn monsters into one-liners.
steps: int 0..pi/2 sin^2 x dx
int -1..1 x^3 cos x dx
int 0..pi/2 sin x/(sin x + cos x) dx
Mean of sin^2(wt) over a period; RMS of A sin(wt).
contracts.hint: sin^2 = (1 - cos 2x)/2. Odd integrand over symmetric limits is 0. King's rule: x -> a + b - x.

contracts.title: Area and signal energy
contracts.context: Energy of a signal is an integral.
steps: Area between y = x^2 and y = x from 0 to 1.
Energy of x(t) = e^(-t) u(t).
contracts.hint: Area = int (top - bottom). E = int |x|^2 dt.

contracts.title: Beta and Gamma functions (JAS 401 Unit I)
contracts.context: Guaranteed exam item in Unit I, purely formula-driven, high marks per hour.
steps: State Gamma(n+1) = n!, Gamma(1/2) = sqrt(pi), B(m,n) = Gamma(m)Gamma(n)/Gamma(m+n).
int 0..inf x^4 e^-x dx
int 0..inf e^(-x^2) dx
int 0..pi/2 sin^4 x dx
contracts.hint: int 0..inf x^(n-1) e^-x dx = Gamma(n). Substitute t = x^2 for the Gaussian. Wallis for sin^4.

contracts.title: Productive struggle: JEE integrals
contracts.context: Two famous hard integrals. Struggle 15-20 minutes each before the hint.
steps: int 0..pi x sin x/(1 + cos^2 x) dx
Then one integral question from JEE Advanced.
contracts.hint: First: King's rule x -> pi - x, then u = cos x. Second: x = tan t, then King's rule on t.

nodes.name: Multiple integrals and vector calculus (JAS 401 Units I-II)
outcomes: Evaluate double and triple integrals, change the order
Switch to polar and spherical coordinates
Compute gradient, divergence, curl, directional derivative
Apply Green, Stokes and Gauss theorems

contracts.title: Vector toolkit (do before Unit II)
contracts.context: Unit II assumes dot product, cross product and unit vectors; no other node teaches them.
steps: a = (1,2,2), b = (2,-1,0): a.b, |a|, unit vector along a, a x b.
Angle between a and b.
Check a x b is perpendicular to both (dot products 0).
contracts.hint: a x b = (a2 b3 - a3 b2, a3 b1 - a1 b3, a1 b2 - a2 b1).
contracts.success_check: a.b = 0 (so 90 deg); |a| = 3; (1,2,2)/3; a x b = (2, 4, -5), dot with a and b both 0.

contracts.title: Double integrals (Cartesian)
contracts.context: Unit I opener.
steps: int 0..1 int 0..x xy dy dx
int 0..2 int 0..1 (x + y) dy dx
contracts.hint: Do the inner integral treating the outer variable as constant.

contracts.title: Change of order of integration
contracts.context: Asked almost every year: sketch the region first.
steps: Evaluate int 0..1 int x..1 e^(y^2) dy dx by reversing the order.
contracts.hint: Region: 0 <= x <= y <= 1. New limits: x from 0 to y, then y from 0 to 1.

contracts.title: Polar coordinates
contracts.context: dA = r dr dtheta.
steps: int over x^2+y^2 <= a^2 of e^-(x^2+y^2) dA
Area of the circle r = a by double integral.
contracts.hint: x^2 + y^2 = r^2 and do not forget the extra r.

contracts.title: Triple integrals and spherical coordinates
contracts.context: dV = r^2 sin(theta) dr dtheta dphi.
steps: Volume of a sphere of radius a.
int over the unit cube of xyz dV.
contracts.hint: Limits r 0..a, theta 0..pi, phi 0..2pi. The cube splits into three single integrals.

contracts.title: Gradient, divergence, curl, directional derivative
contracts.context: Unit II easy marks.
steps: phi = x^2 y + 2xz at (2,-2,3): grad phi, and its directional derivative along (2,-1,-2).
div of F = (x^2 y, yz, xz).
curl of F = (y, -x, 0).
contracts.hint: Normalise the direction vector (length 3).

contracts.title: Line integral and Green's theorem
contracts.context: Unit II: verify or apply Green.
steps: Compute the circulation of (-y dx + x dy) round the unit circle directly and by Green.
contracts.hint: Parametrise x = cos t, y = sin t. Green: dQ/dx - dP/dy = 2.

contracts.title: Gauss divergence and Stokes
contracts.context: Unit II long answer.
steps: Verify Gauss for F = (x,y,z) over the sphere of radius a: compute the surface integral directly and the volume integral of div F.
For F = (-y, x, 0), surface integral of curl F over the upper unit hemisphere (by Stokes).
contracts.hint: On the sphere n = (x,y,z)/a so F.n = a everywhere; div F = 3. Stokes: equals the line integral round the boundary circle.
contracts.success_check: Both sides of Gauss = 4 pi a^3 (surface: a x 4 pi a^2); Stokes gives 2 pi.

contracts.title: Productive struggle: conservative fields (GATE-style)
contracts.context: GATE EC asks this pattern; check math.r.gate2026_ec for a live one.
steps: Is F = (2xy + z^3, x^2, 3xz^2) conservative? Find its potential.
Work done from (0,0,0) to (1,1,1).
contracts.hint: Show curl F = 0, then integrate component by component.
contracts.success_check: Yes; phi = x^2 y + x z^3; work = 2.

nodes.name: Differential equations
outcomes: Solve separable, linear first-order and exact ODEs
Solve constant-coefficient 2nd-order ODEs (CF + PI incl. resonance)
Solve Cauchy-Euler equations
Model RC and RLC circuits
Solve initial value problems with Laplace transforms

contracts.title: Separable equations
contracts.context: The simplest ODEs; watch 3Blue1Brown DE chapter 1 (math.r.yt_3b1b_diffeq) first.
steps: dy/dx = 2y, y(0) = 3
dy/dx = x/y
contracts.hint: Separate y-terms and x-terms, integrate both sides, then use the initial condition.

contracts.title: Linear first order and the RC circuit
contracts.context: Integrating factor e^(int P dx).
steps: dy/dx + y = e^-x, y(0) = 0
RC dv/dt + v = V, v(0) = 0
contracts.hint: IF = e^x for the first.
contracts.success_check: y = x e^-x; v = V(1 - e^(-t/RC)).

contracts.title: Constant-coefficient homogeneous
contracts.context: Auxiliary equation decides everything.
contracts.hint: Real distinct, repeated, pure imaginary, complex pair.
contracts.success_check: c1 e^(2x) + c2 e^(3x); (c1 + c2 x) e^-x; c1 cos 2x + c2 sin 2x; e^-x (c1 cos 2x + c2 sin 2x).

contracts.title: Particular integrals incl. resonance
contracts.context: Classic first-year LA&DE item; also the base of RLC analysis.
steps: y'' + y = x
y'' + y = sin x
contracts.hint: 1/f(D) e^(ax) = e^(ax)/f(a) if f(a) != 0. For resonance multiply by x.

contracts.title: RLC as a second-order ODE
contracts.context: Damping = discriminant.
steps: L q'' + R q' + q/C = 0 with L = 1 H, R = 2 Ohm, C = 1 F: classify and solve.
contracts.hint: Compare R^2 with 4L/C.
contracts.success_check: q'' + 2q' + q = 0: critically damped, q = (c1 + c2 t) e^-t.

contracts.title: Cauchy-Euler equation
contracts.context: Appears in first-year LA&DE papers.

contracts.title: Laplace method for IVPs
contracts.context: Bridge to math.signals_transforms.

contracts.title: Productive struggle: exact and Bernoulli
contracts.context: 15 minutes before the hint.
steps: dy/dx + y = y^2
contracts.hint: Check dM/dy = dN/dx. For Bernoulli put v = 1/y.

nodes.name: Linear algebra
outcomes: Determinants and inverses
Rank, echelon form and consistency of Ax = b
Eigenvalues/eigenvectors, Cayley-Hamilton, diagonalisation
See matrices as transformations
Least squares for data fitting

project.title: Eigenfaces without faces: PCA on Aankhen CSI windows
project.brief: Run numpy PCA on a day of Aankhen CSI amplitude windows, plot variance explained, and check that the top component separates fan-on from fan-off. RF data only.

contracts.title: Determinant and inverse
contracts.context: Warm-up for everything below.
steps: det [[1,2],[3,4]] and the inverse.
contracts.hint: 2x2 inverse: swap diagonal, negate off-diagonal, divide by det.

contracts.title: Rank and consistency
contracts.context: Classic first-year item: classify the solution set; also the base of Unit IV linear systems.
steps: x+y+z=6, x+2y+3z=14, x+4y+7z=30: rank, and all solutions.
contracts.hint: Row-reduce the augmented matrix. Rank < number of unknowns with consistency means infinitely many solutions.
contracts.success_check: Rank 2; z = t, y = 8 - 2t, x = t - 2 (check in equation 3).

contracts.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
contracts.context: Core of PCA, stability and Markov chains.
contracts.hint: det(A - lambda I) = 0, then solve (A - lambda I) v = 0.

contracts.title: Cayley-Hamilton
contracts.context: Classic exam question.
steps: A = [[1,2],[2,1]]: verify Cayley-Hamilton and find A^-1 from it.
contracts.hint: Characteristic polynomial lambda^2 - 2 lambda - 3.

contracts.title: Diagonalisation and powers
contracts.context: Fast powers = fast Markov chains and recurrences.
steps: Diagonalise A = [[2,1],[1,2]] and find A^n.
contracts.hint: A = P D P^-1 with eigenvectors as columns of P.

contracts.title: Matrices as transformations
contracts.context: 3Blue1Brown chapters 1-6: intuition before more rules.
steps: Watch chapters 3 and 6.
Draw what [[0,-1],[1,0]] and [[2,0],[0,1]] do to the unit square.
Explain det as area scaling in one sentence.
contracts.hint: Columns are where i-hat and j-hat land.
contracts.success_check: Rotation by 90 deg; horizontal stretch by 2; det = signed area scale factor, explained in own words.

contracts.title: Least squares fit
contracts.context: Linear regression = the first ML model.
steps: Fit y = a + bx to (0,1), (1,2), (2,4) with the normal equations.
contracts.hint: [[n, sum x],[sum x, sum x^2]] [a,b] = [sum y, sum xy].

contracts.title: Productive struggle: GATE EC eigen tricks
contracts.context: GATE EC asks eigenvalue properties almost every year (math.r.gate2026_ec, math.r.gate2025_ec).
steps: A is 3x3 with eigenvalues 1, 2, 3: det A, trace A, eigenvalues of A^-1 and of A^2 + I.
Then solve every linear-algebra question in the GATE 2026 EC paper and check with the key (math.r.gate2026_ec_key).
contracts.hint: det = product, trace = sum; f(A) has eigenvalues f(lambda).
contracts.success_check: 6; 6; 1, 1/2, 1/3; 2, 5, 10; GATE linear-algebra items attempted and marked against the official key.

nodes.name: Probability and statistics
outcomes: Count outcomes and use addition/multiplication rules
Tell mutually exclusive from independent
Apply conditional probability and Bayes
Work with discrete and continuous random variables, CDFs
Handle joint, marginal and conditional distributions (JAS 401 Unit V)
Summarise data: mean, variance, normal tables

contracts.title: Counting and sample spaces
contracts.context: Unit V starts here.
steps: P(sum = 7) with two dice.
P(at least one six in 4 rolls).
Committees of 3 from 10 people.
contracts.hint: Complement for 'at least one'.

contracts.title: Mutually exclusive vs independent
contracts.context: The most confused pair in the syllabus.
steps: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, P(A and B) = 0.2: independent? mutually exclusive? P(A or B)?
contracts.hint: Independent: P(AB) = P(A)P(B). Mutually exclusive: P(AB) = 0.
contracts.success_check: Independent yes, mutually exclusive no, P(A or B) = 0.7.

contracts.title: Bayes' theorem
contracts.context: Guaranteed Unit V question. Watch math.r.yt_3b1b_bayes first.
steps: Disease prevalence 1%, sensitivity 99%, false-positive rate 5%: P(disease | positive).
Machines make 50/30/20% of output with defect rates 1/2/3%: P(defective) and P(machine 3 | defective).
contracts.hint: Draw a tree; numerator is one branch, denominator is all branches ending in the evidence.

contracts.title: Binomial and Poisson
contracts.context: Bit errors and packet arrivals.
steps: Binomial n = 10, p = 0.2: mean, variance, P(X = 0).
Poisson lambda = 3: P(X = 0).
contracts.hint: Binomial mean np, variance np(1-p).

contracts.title: Continuous random variable and CDF
contracts.context: PDF/CDF are explicitly in the JAS 401 syllabus.
steps: f(x) = kx on [0,2]: find k, the CDF, P(X > 1), E[X].
contracts.hint: Total probability 1 fixes k. F(x) = int f.

contracts.title: Joint, marginal, conditional
contracts.context: Unit V names these three explicitly.
steps: f(x,y) = x + y on the unit square: check it is a pdf, find f_X, f(y|x), and test independence.
contracts.hint: Marginal: integrate out the other variable.
contracts.success_check: Integrates to 1; f_X = x + 1/2; f(y|x) = (x+y)/(x+1/2); not independent.

contracts.title: Descriptive statistics and the normal curve
contracts.context: Needed for ML and lab reports.
steps: Mean, population variance and SD of {2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9}.
State P(|Z| < 1.96).
contracts.hint: Variance = mean of squared deviations.

contracts.title: Productive struggle: classic puzzles
contracts.context: Brilliant-style puzzles for free: Grinstead & Snell exercises (math.r.grinstead_snell) and AoPS Alcumus.
steps: Monty Hall: should you switch?
Birthday problem with 23 people.
Expected number of rolls to get a six.
Then one probability question from JEE Advanced and one from GATE EC.
contracts.hint: Enumerate cases for Monty Hall. Birthday: compute P(all different). Geometric distribution mean 1/p.
contracts.success_check: Switch wins 2/3; ~0.507; 6; written attempts on both exam questions.

nodes.name: Random processes
outcomes: Classify random processes by time index, state and statistical dependence (JAS 401 Unit V)
Compute mean and autocorrelation, test WSS
Use Bernoulli and Poisson processes
Find a Markov chain's stationary distribution
Link autocorrelation to PSD (Wiener-Khinchin)

project.title: Fan fingerprint
project.brief: Estimate the PSD of CSI amplitude with fan on vs off and find the fan peak.

contracts.title: Classification table (exam short answer)
contracts.context: JAS 401 Unit V lists 'types based on time index and on statistical dependence': a safe 5-mark answer.
steps: Make a 2x2 table: discrete/continuous time x discrete/continuous state, one example each.
List by statistical dependence: independent (iid), Markov, stationary (SSS, WSS), ergodic, with one-line definitions.
Recall it blank the next day.
contracts.hint: Bernoulli process, random telegraph signal, thermal noise voltage, sampled noise sequence.
contracts.success_check: Table and definitions reproduced from memory with 4 correct examples.

contracts.title: Mean, autocorrelation, WSS
contracts.context: The standard random-phase sinusoid.
steps: X(t) = A cos(wt + Theta), Theta uniform on [0, 2pi), A constant: mean and R(t, t+tau). WSS?
Now Y(t) = B cos(wt) with B zero-mean, variance s^2: WSS?
contracts.hint: Average over Theta: E[cos(wt + Theta)] = 0. Use cos a cos b = (1/2)[cos(a-b) + cos(a+b)].
contracts.success_check: Mean 0, R = (A^2/2) cos(w tau), WSS; Y: mean 0 but R = s^2 cos(w t1) cos(w t2) depends on t1, t2, so not WSS.

contracts.title: Bernoulli counting process
contracts.context: Bit streams.
steps: S_n = sum of n Bernoulli(p): mean and variance.
contracts.hint: Sum of independent variables: variances add.

contracts.title: Poisson process
contracts.context: Packet and photon arrivals.
steps: Rate 2 per minute: P(no arrival in 1 minute), mean arrivals in 3 minutes, mean inter-arrival time.
contracts.hint: N(t) ~ Poisson(lambda t); inter-arrival ~ exponential(lambda).

contracts.title: Markov chain stationary distribution
contracts.context: Markov = 'based on statistical dependence'.
steps: Two-state chain P = [[0.9, 0.1],[0.5, 0.5]]: find pi.
contracts.hint: Solve pi = pi P with pi1 + pi2 = 1.

contracts.title: Autocorrelation to PSD
contracts.context: Bridge to Digital Communication noise analysis.
steps: R(tau) = e^(-a|tau|): find S(w) by Fourier transform.
contracts.hint: Split the integral at tau = 0.

contracts.title: Project contract: autocorrelation of live CSI
contracts.context: Real data from his own Aankhen board; RF only.
steps: Load 60 s of CSI amplitude for one subcarrier (fan off) and 60 s (fan on).
Compute the sample autocorrelation with numpy for lags 0..200.
Plot both and explain the difference in two sentences.
contracts.hint: Subtract the mean first; R(0) is the variance.
contracts.success_check: Two plots saved; R(0) equals np.var of the series; fan-on shows a periodic ripple at the fan's rate.

nodes.name: Signals and transforms (Fourier, Laplace, Z)
outcomes: Compute Fourier series of standard waves
Use Laplace pairs and properties, invert with partial fractions
Read poles, stability and frequency response
Use Fourier transform pairs
Use the Z-transform for difference equations
Convolve by hand

project.title: FFT of a real signal
project.brief: FFT one minute of Aankhen CSI amplitude, find the fan's spectral line, and design a 1st-order IIR to suppress it.

contracts.title: Fourier series of a square wave
contracts.context: Watch math.r.yt_3b1b_fourier first.
steps: Odd square wave, +1 on (0, pi), -1 on (-pi, 0): find b_n.
contracts.hint: Odd function: only sine terms; b_n = (2/pi) int 0..pi sin(nx) dx.
contracts.success_check: b_n = 4/(n pi) for odd n, 0 for even n.

contracts.title: Laplace pairs and shifting
contracts.context: Watch math.r.yt_3b1b_laplace.
steps: Write L{1}, L{t}, L{e^(at)}, L{sin wt}, L{cos wt} from memory.
L{e^(-2t) sin 3t}
contracts.hint: Multiplying by e^(-2t) replaces s with s + 2.

contracts.title: Inverse Laplace
contracts.context: Uses math.algebra.c06.
contracts.hint: Complete the square: (s+2)^2 + 9, and write s + 3 = (s+2) + 1.

contracts.title: Transfer function of an RC low-pass
contracts.context: Poles = behaviour.
steps: H(s) = 1/(1 + sRC): pole, step response, -3 dB frequency.
contracts.hint: Step response = inverse Laplace of H(s)/s.

contracts.title: Fourier transform pairs
contracts.context: Spectrum of a pulse = bandwidth of a bit.
steps: FT of rect(t/T).
FT of e^(-at) u(t).
What does a time shift do?
contracts.hint: Use sinc(x) = sin(pi x)/(pi x).
contracts.success_check: T sinc(fT); 1/(a + j 2 pi f); multiplies by e^(-j 2 pi f t0) (phase only).

contracts.title: Z-transform and a first-order filter
contracts.context: DSP and the IIR filters inside Aankhen.
steps: Z{a^n u[n]} and its ROC.
y[n] = 0.5 y[n-1] + x[n]: H(z), stability, impulse response.
contracts.hint: Geometric series in z^-1.
contracts.success_check: 1/(1 - a z^-1), |z| > |a|; H = 1/(1 - 0.5 z^-1), stable (pole 0.5 inside unit circle), h[n] = 0.5^n u[n].

contracts.title: Convolution by hand
contracts.context: Output = input * impulse response.
steps: u(t) * e^-t u(t)
contracts.hint: Flip and slide, or multiply the polynomials 1 + 2z + z^2 and 1 + z.

contracts.title: Productive struggle: GATE EC system question
contracts.context: Then do every signals question in math.r.gate2026_ec and mark with math.r.gate2026_ec_key.
steps: H(s) = (s+1)/(s^2 + 5s + 6): poles, stability, impulse response, final value of the step response.
contracts.hint: Partial fractions with cover-up; final value theorem = H(0) for a unit step.

nodes.name: Discrete mathematics
outcomes: Logic and De Morgan (digital design link)
Sets and inclusion-exclusion
Permutations and combinations
Proof by induction
Modular arithmetic and two's complement
Linear recurrences
Graph basics and pigeonhole

contracts.title: Logic and De Morgan
contracts.context: Same algebra as logic gates.
steps: Truth table for p -> q and its contrapositive.
Show not(p and q) = (not p) or (not q).
contracts.hint: p -> q is false only when p is true and q is false.
contracts.success_check: Tables correct; contrapositive identical to p -> q.

contracts.title: Inclusion-exclusion
contracts.context: Counting overlaps.
steps: How many of 1..100 are divisible by 2 or 3?
contracts.hint: |A or B| = |A| + |B| - |A and B|; divisible by both means by 6.

contracts.title: Permutations and combinations
contracts.context: Probability and coding theory need these.
steps: Arrangements of LEVEL.
8-bit strings with exactly three 1s.
8-bit strings with at least one 1.
contracts.hint: Divide by repeats. Complement for at least one.

contracts.title: Induction
contracts.context: The proof pattern behind recursion.
steps: Prove 2^n > n^2 for n >= 5.
contracts.hint: Base case, assume for k, show for k+1.
contracts.success_check: Both proofs complete with base case and step.

contracts.title: Modular arithmetic and two's complement
contracts.context: Hardware arithmetic.
steps: -5 in 8-bit two's complement.
contracts.hint: 7 = 2 mod 5 and 2^4 = 1 mod 5. Invert 00000101 and add 1.

contracts.title: Linear recurrences
contracts.context: Same method as constant-coefficient ODEs.
contracts.hint: Characteristic equation r^2 - 3r + 2 = 0.

contracts.title: Graphs and pigeonhole
contracts.context: Networks, routing, scheduling.
steps: Can 5 vertices all have degree 3?
Why must two of 13 people share a birth month?
Then one Project Euler problem (math.r.project_euler) from the first 20.
contracts.hint: Sum of degrees = 2 x edges, so it must be even.
contracts.success_check: No (sum 15 is odd); 13 people into 12 months; one Project Euler answer accepted.

nodes.name: Numerical methods (JAS 401 Units III-IV)
outcomes: Find roots by bisection, regula falsi and Newton-Raphson
Interpolate with Newton forward/backward, Lagrange and divided differences
Solve linear systems by LU, Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel
Integrate with trapezoidal, Simpson 1/3 and 3/8
Solve ODEs with RK4

project.title: Numerical toolkit
project.brief: Python file implementing all JAS 401 Unit III-IV methods with self-tests against the contract answers.

contracts.title: Bisection
contracts.context: Unit III, pure procedure: tabulate and you get full marks.
steps: f(x) = x^3 - x - 1 on [1,2]: four bisection steps in a table (a, b, mid, f(mid)).
contracts.hint: Keep the half where f changes sign.

contracts.title: Regula falsi
contracts.context: Unit III.
steps: Same f on [1,2]: two regula falsi steps.

contracts.title: Newton-Raphson
contracts.context: Unit III; also how computers take square roots.
steps: sqrt 2 from x0 = 1, three steps.
x^3 - x - 1 = 0 from x0 = 1.5, two steps.

contracts.title: Newton forward and backward interpolation
contracts.context: Unit III: build the difference table once, use it twice.
steps: Data x = 1,2,3,4; y = 1,8,27,64. Build the forward difference table.
Estimate y(1.5) by the forward formula and y(3.5) by the backward formula.

contracts.title: Lagrange and divided differences (unequal intervals)
contracts.context: Unit III.
steps: Points (0,1), (1,3), (3,13): Lagrange polynomial and value at x = 2.
Same points by Newton's divided differences.
contracts.success_check: P(x) = x^2 + x + 1 both ways; P(2) = 7.

contracts.title: Trapezoidal, Simpson 1/3 and 3/8
contracts.context: Unit IV, almost certain to appear.
steps: int 0..1 dx/(1+x^2) with h = 0.25 by trapezoidal and Simpson 1/3.
Same integral with h = 1/3 by Simpson 3/8.
Compare with pi/4 = 0.785398.
contracts.hint: Simpson 1/3 needs an even number of strips; 3/8 needs a multiple of 3.

contracts.title: Gauss-Seidel, Jacobi, LU
contracts.context: Unit IV.
steps: 10x+y+z=12, x+10y+z=12, x+y+10z=12: two Gauss-Seidel iterations from (0,0,0) and one Jacobi iteration.
Doolittle LU of [[2,3],[4,7]].
contracts.hint: Gauss-Seidel uses each new value immediately; Jacobi waits for the whole sweep.

contracts.title: RK4
contracts.context: Unit IV: one full step must be perfect.
steps: dy/dx = x + y, y(0) = 1, h = 0.1: one RK4 step.
Compare with the exact 2e^x - x - 1.

contracts.title: Project contract: code the methods
contracts.context: Turn Units III-IV into Python so every hand answer has a checker.
steps: Write bisection, newton, simpson13, rk4 in one Python file.
Run them on c01, c03, c06 and c08 inputs.
Print hand vs code side by side.
contracts.hint: Keep each function under 15 lines; no libraries except math.
contracts.success_check: All four functions reproduce the success values above to 4 decimals.

contracts.title: RK4 for a second-order ODE (system form)
contracts.context: Unit IV names second-order and simultaneous ODEs explicitly.
steps: One RK4 step with h = 0.1 for both y and z, in a table.
Compare with sin(0.1) and cos(0.1).
contracts.hint: Compute k1 for y and z together, then k2 for both using the k1 values, and so on.

nodes.name: Optimisation for ML
outcomes: Test convexity and second-order conditions
Find critical points with gradient and Hessian
Run gradient descent and pick a learning rate
Solve constrained problems with Lagrange multipliers
Derive least squares as an optimisation
Backpropagate through one neuron

project.title: Regression from scratch
project.brief: numpy gradient descent vs closed form on Aankhen features, with a learning-rate sweep plot.

contracts.title: Convexity check
contracts.context: Convex = any local minimum is global.
steps: f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 5: minimum and value, convex?
contracts.hint: f'' >= 0 everywhere means convex.

contracts.title: Gradient and Hessian
contracts.context: Multivariable version.
steps: f(x,y) = x^2 + 3y^2 - 2x + 6y: critical point, Hessian, minimum value.
contracts.hint: Hessian positive definite means a minimum.

contracts.title: Gradient descent by hand
contracts.context: Watch math.r.yt_3b1b_gradient.
steps: f(x) = x^2, x0 = 4: three steps with lr 0.25, two with lr 1.0, two with lr 1.25.
contracts.hint: x <- x - lr x 2x.

contracts.title: Lagrange multipliers
contracts.context: Constrained optimisation, the base of SVMs.
steps: Maximise xy subject to x + y = 10.
Minimise x^2 + y^2 subject to x + 2y = 5.
contracts.hint: grad f = lambda grad g.

contracts.title: Least squares as optimisation
contracts.context: Ties to math.linear_algebra.c07.
steps: Differentiate ||Ax - b||^2 and set it to zero.
contracts.success_check: A^T A x = A^T b derived.

contracts.title: Backprop through one neuron
contracts.context: The chain rule is all of deep learning.
steps: y = sigmoid(wx + b), L = (y - t)^2/2, w = 0.5, b = 0, x = 2, t = 1: compute dL/dw.
contracts.hint: sigmoid' = sigmoid (1 - sigmoid).

contracts.title: Project contract: gradient descent regression
contracts.context: Real ML on his own data.
steps: Fit linear regression with numpy gradient descent on 3 Aankhen features.
Sweep lr over 5 values and plot loss curves.
Compare with the normal-equation solution.
contracts.hint: Standardise features first or the learning rate will not behave.
contracts.success_check: Loss falls monotonically for the chosen lr; weights match the closed form within 1e-3.

placement.how: Take the 30-question diagnostic on paper, no calculator, 45 minutes max. Mark each item right/wrong. Skip, do not guess.
placement.place_at: The lowest level (1-10) where you got fewer than 2 out of every 3 items right. Every node at or below that level starts at contract c01; nodes above it stay locked until their prereqs pass the mastery gate.
placement.retake: Retake the diagnostic every 4 weeks; never study from its answers.

library_maths_day_180min: 15 min spaced review: due flashcards + 3 old problems from the error log
60 min new contract(s) with worked-example fading
45 min productive-struggle set (hard problems, hint ladder)
30 min interleaved mixed set of 6-10 problems from all unlocked nodes
5 min: log score, add misses to error log, make 2-5 new cards
evening_home_30_45min: 10-20 min one short contract or redo of yesterday's misses
daily_session.why_evening_matters: With maths only one library day in five, the evening reviews are what keeps the spacing intervals alive between library days.

spacing.rule: A problem or card you get right moves to the next interval; a miss returns it to day 1. Use Anki with FSRS (math.r.anki, math.r.fsrs) for formula and method cards; use the error log for whole problems.
spacing.evidence: Cepeda et al. 2008: for tests 7/35/70/350 days away the best review gaps were about 3/8/12/27 days (43/23/17/8% of the delay). Distributed practice is one of two 'high utility' techniques in Dunlosky et al. 2013.

retrieval.rule: Every session starts from a blank page: write the formula/method/definition before looking. Rereading notes does not count as study time.
retrieval.evidence: Testing beat restudy at 1 week (Roediger & Karpicke 2006); meta-analyses: testing vs restudy g = 0.50 (Rowland 2014) and practice testing g ~ 0.5-0.6 (Adesope et al. 2017); retrieval beat concept mapping (Karpicke & Blunt 2011).

interleaving.rule: Once a node has 2+ finished contracts, its practice sets mix problem types from that node and older nodes. Before solving, write which method the problem needs. Expect practice scores to drop; that is the point.
interleaving.evidence: Rohrer & Taylor 2007: mixed practice scored 60% vs 89% during practice but 63% vs 20% on the test a week later. Rohrer et al. 2020 (787 students, 54 classes, preregistered RCT): 61% vs 38% on an unannounced test, d = 0.83.

productive_struggle.rule: Each hard problem gets 15 minutes of genuine attempt (written, any idea counts) before the first hint. Hint ladder: (1) name the method, (2) first step, (3) full worked solution, then redo the problem from blank the next day.
productive_struggle.evidence: Sinha & Kapur 2021 meta-analysis (53 studies, 166 comparisons): problem solving before instruction beat instruction-first, g = 0.36, up to 0.58 when the struggle is well designed. It did not help grade 2-5 children or weak prior knowledge with no follow-up instruction, so the struggle always ends with a worked solution.

stages: S1: study a complete worked example and explain each step aloud
S2: same type, last step blank
worked_example_fading.advance_when: 2 correct in a row at the current stage.
worked_example_fading.stop_when: You solve S4 problems correctly; from then on examples slow you down (expertise reversal).
worked_example_fading.evidence: Sweller & Cooper 1985 (algebra); Renkl et al. 2002 and Atkinson, Renkl & Merrill 2003 (fading steps helps transfer); Kalyuga et al. 2003 (examples help novices, hurt experts).

mental_maths.rule: Timed, mixed, no calculator, scored. Target 18/20 in 5 minutes before moving the sprint up a difficulty.

fields: error type: concept | method choice | algebra/sign slip | arithmetic | misread
error_log.rule: Every miss goes in. Sign slips and arithmetic errors are counted separately because they are his main mark-loser.

rules.mastery_gate: A node passes when an interleaved mixed set of 10 problems from it scores >= 8/10 on two different days at least 3 days apart, with no worked examples open.
rules.xp: Contract xp is roughly its minutes; productive-struggle and project contracts carry extra. XP counts only when the success_check is met. Daily streak needs the mental sprint + reviews, not new material.
rules.honest_timeline: The 16 nodes total about 385 hours; at about 6 hours a week that is over a year, so an exam plan (served privately by the app) may override the node order until a given exam.
